headline: Fractional CMO Companies: 7 Top Options (2026)
image: [IMAGE: Comparison of fractional CMO companies for growing businesses]
description: Compare the best fractional CMO companies for startups and growth-stage businesses. Vetted options, real pricing, and what to look for before you hire.

mainEntity.name: How much do fractional CMO companies charge?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most fractional CMO companies charge between $5,000 and $20,000 per month, depending on the provider, scope, and seniority level. MarketerHire engagements typically run $7,000-$10,000/month. Enterprise-focused firms like Chief Outsiders can exceed $25,000/month. Month-to-month contracts are standard at marketplace-style providers.

mainEntity.name: How many hours per week does a fractional CMO work?

acceptedAnswer.text: Fractional CMOs typically work 10-20 hours per week, spread across two to four days. The exact commitment depends on company stage and scope. Early-stage startups building marketing from scratch may need the higher end. Companies with existing teams that need strategic oversight often work with 10-12 hours weekly.

mainEntity.name: Are fractional CMOs a good fit for startups?

acceptedAnswer.text: Fractional CMOs are often the best fit for startups. Most companies between seed and Series C need marketing leadership but cannot justify a $250,000+ full-time CMO salary. A fractional CMO brings the same caliber of strategic thinking at 30-50% of the cost, with flexibility to scale as the company grows.

mainEntity.name: How long should you work with a fractional CMO?

acceptedAnswer.text: Plan for a minimum of six months to see meaningful results. The first month covers audit and strategy. Months two and three focus on execution setup. Months four through six generate measurable outcomes. Some companies work with a fractional CMO for 12-18 months, transitioning to a full-time hire when the role justifies it.

mainEntity.name: How do you vet a fractional CMO company?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ask five questions: What is your CMO acceptance rate? Can I see case studies from my industry? What happens if the match doesn't work? What is your average time to first match? How do you measure CMO performance? Companies that answer with specific data — not generalities — are worth evaluating further.
